rawCandidates.selectionReason: Studio booking page with class calendar, tabs, availability states, and a direct book action.
Empty availability state is useful for class schedule expectations and no-slot messaging.
Pilates-adjacent membership hero with app preview and category-specific imagery.
Featured studio grid shows how to present venue proof and class categories without a heavy hero.
Venue-detail page with map, appointment tab, safety area, and direct contact facts.
Fitness studio software landing page gives a strong anti-reference for admin-side claims.
Booking-first wellness search hero with service, place, date, and time controls.
Compact customer menu and appointment utilities are useful for mobile booking behavior.
Location and membership benefit page helps separate intro class, studio nearby, and membership paths.
Membership savings section maps to recurring small-group membership explanation.
Reactivation page mixes flexibility, class times, studio safety, and wellness categories.
Studio-space section shows how to discuss ambience and group dynamics without body-transformation claims.
Plan cards and credit model are useful as a warning and a membership comparison reference.
Dense collage hero is useful as an anti-reference for generic fitness marketplace energy.
Two-column upgrade form is useful as a membership signup anti-reference for over-financialized onboarding.
Dark premium plan page is a useful warning against loud entertainment-style membership design.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Make the first decision a class-path choice: reformer intro, private session, or small-group membership.
Use tabs for classes, private sessions, and pricing so the visitor can compare paths without reading a long story.
Class rows need class name, time, room or format, capacity if verified, and a clear book action.
Show available, unavailable, selected date, empty day, and booking confirmation states.
Let the visitor choose date and class before requesting full account or payment details.
Calendar cells, class rows, and book buttons need labels that work for keyboard and screen-reader users.

bannedUses: Do not copy Time2book branding, beach image, fake studio name, powered-by footer, exact schedule data, or SaaS admin shell.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: A generous booking hero can foreground service, location, date, and time without a hard-sell fitness promise.
The hero search should collapse into a stacked mobile booking module with one dominant CTA.
Primary CTA should stay book-focused, with private-session enquiry as a secondary path.
Keep lead capture short: preferred path, date/time interest, contact, and optional experience level.
Use London area, UK date/time conventions, and studio-specific class terms only when source-backed.

bannedUses: Do not copy Fresha's gradient, marketplace counts, beauty language, app-download CTA, customer menu, or exact search component.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Separate intro, private, and membership copy so beginners do not feel pushed into the wrong commitment.
Use calm, precise movement language; avoid body-shape, weight-loss, and transformation claims.
If real studio photos are unavailable, use equipment, floor-plan, class-path, and reformer-line artifacts instead of stock bodies.
Use class structure, instructor process, and booking clarity as proof until real reviews or credentials are approved.
Body, medical, pregnancy, injury, and instructor qualification claims must remain absent unless directly verified.

bannedUses: Do not copy ClassPass marketplace positioning, phone mockups, reviews, rating stars, global access claims, or body imagery.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Location, class categories, safety/cleanliness, and clear contact routes can act as grounded trust cues.
Expose reformer intro, private session, membership, location, and booking path in visible and agent-readable metadata.
Venue detail should not depend on heavy map scripts or large galleries before real media is approved.
Tokenize venue fact rows, schedule rows, tabs, chips, and secondary CTA widths for repeatable preview builds.

bannedUses: Do not copy Crunch Gym details, map, rating, social handles, safety claims, or gym-chain voice.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Keep action color disciplined and avoid making the studio feel like a generic blue fitness app.
Membership sections need generous breathing room so plans feel calm rather than salesy.
Use clean plan surfaces and subtle dividers instead of stacked promotional cards.
Reserve depth for selected plan or booking module; keep the rest flat and quiet.

bannedUses: Do not copy ClassPass credit economics, discount claims, global membership language, blue CTA identity, or fake savings.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Use compact, confident headings for sections like intro class, private work, and membership without oversized gym hype.
Use simple image and equipment frames; avoid rounded card overload.
Studio ambience can be represented through reformer silhouettes, room rhythm, and equipment details when real photos are missing.
Icons should clarify beginner, private, group, time, equipment, and location rather than decorate.

bannedUses: Do not copy yoga-studio photography, ambience promises, tribe language, or unverified studio-space claims.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: A controlled collage can show class path variety, but should be replaced by safe generated reformer/equipment artifacts if photos are unapproved.
Motion should be limited to tab changes, class-path selection, or booking step reveal.
Use flexibility copy for schedule and commitment, not body outcome claims.
Photo or artifact grids must collapse below the booking path on mobile.

bannedUses: Do not copy reactivation offers, COVID/safety claims, marketplace photography, phone app mockups, or 'feel great' body-result language.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Membership enquiry can use plan intent plus contact details, without requiring payment in the first preview.
Plan cards need selected, default, unavailable, loading, and compare states.
Use GBP and London language only when pricing or location is source-backed; otherwise leave pricing out.
Membership, cancellation, credit, and recurring-payment claims must be omitted until the business supplies real terms.

bannedUses: Do not copy ClassPass credits, prices, default-plan labels, cancellation terms, or global booking benefits.

antiReferences.rejectionReason: Fitness studio software marketing is operator-facing SaaS, not a customer-facing Pilates studio booking page.
Dense marketplace collage and broad fitness/beauty positioning would drown the local Pilates decision.
Financial upgrade checkout patterns make membership feel transactional and off-category for a calm studio page.
Loud dark entertainment subscription styling conflicts with calm movement, beginner trust, and local studio clarity.

remixDirection.summary: A calm booking-first Pilates page that splits reformer intro, private session, and small-group membership paths, uses a light schedule module as proof, and replaces body-transformation imagery with equipment, studio-rhythm, and class-path artifacts.
selectedMoves: Time2book class calendar discipline, rebuilt as customer-facing reformer intro and private-session booking.
Fresha booking hero clarity for service, date, and time choice without beauty-marketplace claims.
ClassPass venue/detail logic for studio facts, location, and class categories, stripped of marketplace proof.
ClassPass membership comparison patterns, rewritten as source-safe enquiry paths without fake pricing.
Quiet equipment-led visuals instead of stock bodies, transformation claims, or generic gym energy.
explicitRejects: No invented reviews, ratings, instructor credentials, injury/medical claims, body-shape outcomes, prices, or membership terms.
No copied ClassPass/Fresha/Time2book brand systems, marketplace metrics, global claims, or app-download CTAs.
No exact layout copy, dashboard UI, or photo-heavy fitness collage unless the business supplies approved photos.
